problem: RL-based exploration with atomic actions is data-inefficient, and prior hierarchical methods (ANS) only have a single option (navigate to a point), while frontier methods never learn and always rotate/navigate in a fixed pattern.
motivation: Robots must map new environments quickly under a limited step budget. A 'look-around' rotation is often cheaper than moving, so letting the policy interleave navigation and look-around should give higher coverage and more compact trajectories.
key_idea: Use an option-critic architecture with two high-level options (navigate to a selected frontier via path planning, or look around by a chosen angle) trained with RL on coverage-gain reward.
insight: Adding the look-around option to frontier navigation improves coverage: full model vs option-disabled is 0.95 vs 0.87 on Gibson at 1k steps and 0.71 vs 0.64 on Matterport3D. Macro-actions with classic path planning beat atomic actions by a wide margin (0.95 vs 0.75 Gibson), and the learned agent looks around first and again when most of the scene is explored. Frontier goals help most on large scenes: frontier-only reaches 0.50 vs 0.71 on MP3D, while arbitrary-point goals match the full model on MP3D at 1k steps.
method: Map input: five 512x512 maps (occupancy, explored, trajectory, current location, frontier) built from GT depth and pose; a 7-layer strided CNN plus 2 FC layers encode them and are concatenated with ResNet18 RGB features.
Two options: ω1 navigates to a selected frontier point using fast-marching path planning; ω2 rotates in place by a predicted angle. Each has its own action space (x,y vs angle).

Option-critic: option-value V(s,ω), intra-option policies (A2C-style advantage gradient), termination functions β trained to increase termination when the option is suboptimal; the policy over options is greedy argmax of V.
TD target: r + γ((1-β)V(s',ω) + β max V), γ=0.99.
Reward: increase in coverage divided by total scene area.
Training: each macro-action lasts 50 steps; 8 parallel simulators; update every 20 macro-actions with a buffer of 20 trajectories; 750 training episodes.

setting.backbone: CNN map encoder + ResNet18 with option-critic heads (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 750 episodes on Gibson (or Matterport3D) training scenes, no extra data
setting.observation: RGB-D 256x256 plus ground-truth pose; occupancy/explored/frontier maps
setting.action_space: Macro-actions: frontier goal (x,y) with path planning, or in-place rotation angle; 1000 total steps per episode
setting.privileged: ground-truth pose/localization and simulator depth used as inputs

results: The full method reaches 95% coverage on Gibson and 71% on Matterport3D at 1000 steps, beating frontier (0.88/0.50), atomic (0.75/0.27) and the option-disabled ablation (0.87/0.64). It ties the arbitrary-point method on MP3D at 1k steps (0.71) and beats it on Gibson (0.92), and gives shorter, cleaner trajectories.
limitations: Uses ground-truth pose and depth; the baselines are simplified (no SLAM or local policy).
Gains over the arbitrary-point method are small; it ties on MP3D at 1k steps and is not significantly better on large scenes.
Only two options and a greedy option policy; no real-robot tests.
